user.title: Add heating system
user.description: What should the system be called, and how many controllers does it have? Each controller has its own IP address.

data_description.name: Applies to the whole system. A place fits better than a boiler name, such as "Basement" or "Barn".

system.title: Controller {nummer} of {anzahl}
system.description: Label, IP address, access and service password.

data_description.username: By default the system knows “USER” and “Service”. “Service” also returns the expert parameters. A different name can be entered.
data_description.label: Appears in front of every device, such as "Basement · Buffer tank". A place fits better than a boiler name.

scope.title: Choose scope
scope.description:
Found:

{gefunden}

Which levels should be included? Info and operator level are always included. Service and factory level contain expert parameters. The choice applies to all controllers at first and can be changed per controller later.

After finishing, HeatNexus reads the system in full in the background. Depending on the system this takes 30 to 120 seconds, and further entities keep appearing meanwhile. A notification tells you when everything is there.

data.zeitwerte: Create system clock and system date
data.lon: Read values from the LON bus
data.lon_grundumfang: Add basic values from the LON bus

data_description.levels: Info: readings. Operator: mode, setpoints, programs. Service: heating curve, limits. Factory: combustion control, drives.
data_description.enable_advanced: Unchecked, the entities are created but stay disabled and cause no polling.
data_description.writable_advanced: Unchecked, these parameters are shown read-only.
data_description.update_interval: How often the system is queried. The value applies to fast values (thermostat, temperatures, pumps); slower values keep their own spacing — 2 minutes for operating values, 15 minutes for meters. Recommended: 30 seconds for one system, 60 seconds for several or for systems with many datapoints.
data_description.dashboard: Adds a “Heating” dashboard to the sidebar that builds itself from the discovered devices.
data_description.panel: Adds a “HeatNexus” entry to the sidebar with a plant diagram, status, heating circuits and quick actions.
data_description.zeitwerte: The controller's own clock. Without the tick they are created disabled; all other time and date fields are unaffected.
data_description.lon: The controller keeps a full bus address space alongside the datapoints. For a deep look: fan speed, lambda probe heating, pellet stock and everything else. On PuroWIN and Infinity it adds little, because the same values already exist as datapoints.
data_description.lon_grundumfang: Fetches pump, mixer and the boiler's core readings from the bus where the system has no datapoint for them — otherwise they are missing from the diagram. No duplicates: where a datapoint exists, it wins.

reconfigure.description: Enter the new address of the system. Devices, entities and history are kept.

data_description.username: USER sees info and operator level, Service additionally the specialist parameters. Changing it re-reads the plant.

data_description.update_interval: How often the system is queried. The value applies to fast values (thermostat, temperatures, pumps); slower values keep their own spacing — 2 minutes for operating values, 15 minutes for meters. Recommended: 30 seconds for one system, 60 seconds for several or for systems with many datapoints.
data_description.dashboard: Adds a “Heating” dashboard to the sidebar that builds itself from the discovered devices.
data_description.panel: Adds a “HeatNexus” entry to the sidebar with a plant diagram, status, heating circuits and quick actions.
data_description.meldung_einlesen: Shows a notification while HeatNexus reads the plant.
data_description.vorlagen: Which blueprints appear under Settings → Automations. A blueprint an automation still uses stays in place.
data_description.aussentemperatur: Which sensor counts as the outside temperature in the header. Empty: HeatNexus finds it in the plant itself.
data_description.hilfe: Adds a „?“ next to cards and controls that explains what a value means and what an action does.
data_description.sprache: Where the datapoint names come from. With “Automatic” they stay German and the interface follows the language of Home Assistant.

data.label: Controller name
data.ids_anpassen: Rename entity IDs to the new name
data.modulpumpe: Pump connected to the pump/relay module
data.zeitwerte: Create system clock and system date
data.lon: Read values from the LON bus
data.lon_grundumfang: Add basic values from the LON bus
data.marken_status: Put these labels into the system status

data_description.label: Appears in front of every device, such as "Basement · Buffer tank". A place fits better than a boiler name.
data_description.ids_anpassen: Renames the IDs that start with the previous name. Automations, scripts and your own dashboards that use the old IDs need to be updated afterwards.
data_description.levels: Info: readings. Operator: mode, setpoints, programs. Service: heating curve, limits. Factory: combustion control, drives.
data_description.enable_advanced: Unchecked, the entities are created but stay disabled and cause no polling.
data_description.writable_advanced: Unchecked, these parameters are shown read-only.
data_description.username: USER sees info and operator level, Service additionally the specialist parameters. Changing it re-reads the plant.
data_description.kesselart: Which appliance the plant diagram draws. Affects the drawing only – no entity, no value changes.
data_description.kesselwert: Which second value is shown at the boiler. The ember bed still follows the output; if none is reported it falls back to the combustion chamber temperature.
data_description.modulpumpe: Only with the tick does the module's pump appear in the diagram. The module reports a speed even when nothing is wired to it; the module itself and its lamps are shown either way.
data_description.zeitwerte: The controller's own clock. Without the tick they are created disabled; all other time and date fields are unaffected.
data_description.lon: Also reads the bus address space of the controller: fan speed, lambda probe heating, pellet stock and whatever is only available there. On PuroWIN and Infinity this adds little, because the same values already come as data points.
data_description.lon_grundumfang: Reads pump, mixing valve and the core boiler values from the bus where the system does not provide them as data points; otherwise they are missing in the diagram. "Read values from the LON bus" does not need to be switched on for this. Where the data point exists, the data point applies.
data_description.zusatzgruppen: Values HeatNexus derives from existing counters and states: running times (today, since the last start), counters (starts, consumption, heat) and the running duration. Unticked ones are created disabled. With “Individuell”, pressing OK opens a second step listing the individual values.
data_description.marken: Each selected label becomes its own card in the overview. Anyone who does not need one hides it there. What someone sees in a card depends on their permissions in Home Assistant.
data_description.marken_status: Values of these labels appear in the system status instead of their own card. Only labels shown above can be selected.

zusatzwerte.title: Derived values in detail
zusatzwerte.description: Tick the values that should be enabled.

steuerung_neu.title: Add controller
steuerung_neu.description: Another controller of this heating system. After saving, HeatNexus reloads and reads it in; the existing controllers stay unchanged.

data_description.username: Out of the box the system knows "USER" and "Service". "Service" also delivers the specialist parameters.
data_description.label: Appears in front of every device, such as "Basement · Buffer tank". A place fits better than a boiler name.

steuerung_entfernen.title: Remove controller
steuerung_entfernen.description: Which controller should be removed from this heating system?

steuerung_entfernen_bestaetigen.title: Remove controller
steuerung_entfernen_bestaetigen.description:
**{anlage}** is removed together with everything attached to it:

- {geraete} devices with their entities and history
- Automations: {automatiken}. Their interventions on the controller are reverted.
- Heat sources: {quellen}

This cannot be undone. If the controller is added again later, it is read in from scratch.

data.verstanden: I understand and want to remove the controller

error.bestaetigung_fehlt: Please confirm that the controller should be removed with everything attached to it.
error.already_configured: This address is already part of this heating system.
error.invalid_auth: Login rejected - check the service password

abort.steuerung_hinzugefuegt: The controller has been added. HeatNexus reloads and reads it in.
abort.steuerung_entfernt: The controller has been removed. HeatNexus reloads.
abort.letzte_steuerung: The last controller cannot be removed. To remove the whole heating system, delete the entry.

options.schwelle: Threshold (value above or below a limit)

nicht_erreichbar.title: {anlage} cannot be reached

sprache_neustart.title: Language changed – restart required
sprache_neustart.description:
The language of the labels was changed. HeatNexus already reads the new names from the controller; they become visible after a restart of Home Assistant.

This message then disappears by itself.

confirm.title: Remove entities without a datapoint
confirm.description:
The system no longer provides a value for {anzahl} entities. They are already disabled and cost no request.

Removing them discards your own name, icon, area and history. If the system delivers the value again, the entity is created anew.

abort.nicht_geladen: The system is not loaded right now. Please try again later.

automatik_sicherheit.title: Automation {heizkreis}: return to program failed
automatik_sicherheit.description:
For safety, the automation tried to return the heating circuit **{heizkreis}** to its program. The controller rejected this twice.

Please check the operating mode of the heating circuit and set it manually. This message disappears as soon as the controller accepts an intervention of the automation again.

automatik_ruecknahme.title: Automation {heizkreis}: undo failed
automatik_ruecknahme.description:
When the automation was switched off or removed, the controller rejected undoing its interventions on the heating circuit **{heizkreis}**. The heating circuit may still be set to hot water only or run at a lowered setpoint.

Please check the operating mode and setpoint of the heating circuit and set them manually. This message disappears as soon as an undo succeeds.

user.title: System
user.description: Which system does the heat source belong to?

quelle.title: Heat source
quelle.description: The source appears in the diagram of {anlage}. The condition decides when it delivers heat.

data_description.quelle: The value that decides about the source.
data_description.pumpe: Draws an impeller in the pipe of the source while it delivers heat.

regel.title: Condition
regel.description: When does the source deliver heat? {quelle} decides.

data_description.zustaende: Only these states count as delivering, every other one as off. If one is missing from the list, type it in.
data_description.gegen: Its value is subtracted from the first entity.
data_description.ein: From this value the source counts as delivering.
data_description.aus: Only below this it counts as off again. Empty means the same value.

error.bedingung_unvollstaendig: The condition is incomplete. Threshold and difference need a switch-on value, difference also a second entity.

abort.zu_viele: The diagram cannot hold more heat sources.

wert_abgelehnt.message: The system rejected the value for {oid} (HTTP {status}).

betriebswahl_unbekannt.message: The operating mode is not known yet. Please wait until the system has been read.

keine_anlage_zum_einlesen.message: No system is set up that could be read in again.

zu_viele_schaltpunkte.message: At most {hoechstens} switching points per block, {anzahl} were given.

kein_zeitprogramm.message: This entity is not a writable schedule.

antwortet_nicht.message: The system {anlage} repeatedly does not respond: {fehler}

keine_werte.message: The system {anlage} has not delivered any values yet: {fehler}

keine_anlage_im_eintrag.message: The configuration entry contains no system.

rediscover.name: Detect system again
rediscover.description: Discards the stored discovery state and reads the system in again completely (data points and devices). Needed for example after changes to the heating or when new heating circuits were added. Takes longer once and then reports per system how many entities, polled data points and schedules were found.

set_current_temp_compensation.name: Set comfort correction
set_current_temp_compensation.description: Shifts the measured room temperature of a heating circuit by a fixed amount. Meant for sensors that permanently read too warm or too cold because of where they hang.

compensation.name: Correction
compensation.description: Added to the measured room temperature.

meldungen_loeschen.name: Clear message list
meldungen_loeschen.description: Clears the message list that HeatNexus keeps for a system. The system does not provide this list through its interface, so only the collection in Home Assistant is cleared, not the fault memory on the operating unit. Messages pending there stay and must be reset on the device as usual.

set_vorgabe.name: Set temporary setpoint
set_vorgabe.description: Sets a temporary room temperature setpoint for a heating circuit, the same one the system calls "Eco / Comfort". Afterwards the circuit returns to its operating mode by itself; the schedules stay unchanged. If the circuit is on standby or hot water mode, it switches to a heating program for the duration and back afterwards.

temperature.name: Temperature
temperature.description: Room temperature that applies during the setpoint.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: How long the setpoint applies. 0 ends a running setpoint immediately.

set_time_program.name: Set schedule
set_time_program.description: Writes a heating or hot water schedule (target: a schedule sensor of HeatNexus). Either simplified with switch_points (plus optional weekdays, daily by default) or with blocks for full control (several weekday groups, for example Mon–Fri and Sat–Sun).

switch_points.name: Switching points
switch_points.description: List of switching points with time and value. time as HH:MM, value = target temperature. Applies to the block from weekdays.

weekdays.name: Weekdays
weekdays.description: Weekdays for the switching points (Mo Tu We Th Fr Sa Su or Mo Di Mi Do Fr Sa So). Default: daily.

blocks.name: Blocks (advanced)
blocks.description: Full program structure as a list of blocks, each with weekdays and switch_points. Overrides switch_points/weekdays when given.

dashboard_ausgeben.name: Export dashboard as YAML
dashboard_ausgeben.description: Returns the bundled dashboard as YAML text. It is rebuilt every time it is opened and therefore cannot be edited. With this text you create a dashboard of your own: add a new dashboard, open the raw configuration editor, paste the text.
